newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Maystadt - German EMU remark unimportant.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Maystadt - German EMU remark unimportant.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt on Monday played down comments by a leading German politician who said Belgium should not be admitted to the single currency when it is first launched.
"That comment by Glos has no importance whatsoever. If Hans Tietmeyer of the Bundesbank said this, I would be worried," Maystadt told Belgian daily De Morgen.

On Saturday, Michael Glos, parliamentary leader of Germany's Christian Social Union (CSU), was quoted as saying in Focus magazine that Belgium, Italy and Spain should not be allowed to join the first wave of European economic and monetary union.
The CSU is the conservative Bavarian-based sister party of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, and a junior partner in the Bonn coalition.
"We must definitely be part of EMU, because Belgium is one of the most stable countries in Europe from a financial point of view," Maystadt said.

He added that one should not focus on state debt alone but also at Belgium's low inflation and long-term yields, the strength of the Belgian franc, the reduction of total debt and of the state deficit, which is close to three percent of GDP.
On Friday, the Belgian government said the 1996 deficit ended at 3.4 percent of GDP, down from 4.1 percent but above its 3.0 percent target. The 1997 target is 2.9 percent.
Total Belgian government debt fell to 130.2 of GDP at the end of 1996, from 133.7 percent at the end of 1995. Belgium's debt/GDP ratio is the highest in the EU.
